title: Runbook Templetizer — typed inputs, safe replay, and idempotent adminlets
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a reusable runbook templatizer that turns human-run runbooks into parameterized, typed adminlets that can be executed as tasks by support engineers and automated playflows. The goal is safer operator actions: each adminlet should accept a typed schema for inputs, validate and sanitize before execution, support a dry-run mode, be idempotent where possible, and emit structured telemetry and audit events for postmortems and cost attribution.
acceptance_criteria: CS1: Engineers can define a runbook template with an OpenAPI-like input schema and markdown body in the new templatizer UI or via a YAML file in the repo.
CS2: Adminlets created from templates run in 'dry-run' mode and produce a non-destructive preview for approval flows.
CS3: Execution API enforces input types, performs sanitizer hooks, and returns a deterministic execution plan before mutation steps run.
CS4: All executions emit structured telemetry (event_type, template_id, inputs_hash, outcome, duration, user_id) to the ops-metrics pipeline and an audit entry in the compliance log.
CS5: Runbooks declare idempotency hints; for non-idempotent steps there is an optional 'compensating' step that can be wired to the templating engine.
CS6: Support engineers can invoke a template via Console or CLI, pass approved inputs, and the run displays a replayable execution trace for later re-run in a sandbox environment.
CS7: Unit and e2e tests cover schema validation, dry-run outputs, telemetry emissions, and replay correctness.
CS8: Documentation and a migration script exist for converting 10 high-frequency runbooks into templates as examples.
CS9: Security review completed and SRE runbook annotated for emergency bypass with required approvals.
CS10: Feature gated behind 'adminlets-beta' flag for 1 month before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Backend: Extend runbook service to accept templates stored as YAML with input JSON Schema (subset) and body steps using a simple DSL. Store rending artifacts as immutable template versions.
Validation: Use JSON Schema Draft-07 subset for typed inputs and add sanitizer hooks that run in a sandboxed Python worker.

Execution: Execution engine will first run a 'plan' pass that validates inputs, expands steps, and computes side-effect-free checks. Only after plan approval will mutation steps be executed by orchestrator.
Telemetry: Emit a single 'adminlet.execution' event per run with structured payload. Add 'adminlet.plan' for dry-run previews.
Idempotency: Encourage step authors to mark steps as 'safe' or provide compensating actions. Provide utilities for generating resource-idempotent wrappers.
UI: Console will show template gallery, input form generated from schema, preview plan, and an activity timeline of replays.
CLI: Add 'rwk' subcommand for quick invocation, benchmarking and dry-run output. Tie to SSO-mapped user identity for audit.
Permissions: Integrate with RBAC so templates can be restricted to role or team; require 'runbook.execute' permission and 'runbook.approve' for bypasses.
Safety: All mutation steps run in a restricted token context with explicit allowed scopes; emergency bypass requires two approvers recorded in audit.
Migration: Provide a script to convert existing markdown runbooks in the repo to draft templates with heuristics for inputs (flags, placeholders).
Performance: Plan pass should be capped at 2s median; full execution SLO depends on steps but overall orchestration overhead target is <120ms.
Rollback: Execution engine will checkpoint after each step enabling per-step retry and compensating-run hooks.
Testing: Provide a fake-ops harness that simulates downstream services to validate idempotency and compensating behavior.
Observability: Add per-template dashboards (count, success_rate, avg_duration, fail_reason) in Console and integrate with Alerting team metrics.
Safety-Rollout: Feature-gate and enable in 'support-alpha' workspace first before org-wide enablement.
Notes: Consider future extension to allow scheduling and event-triggered runs (post-incident automatic triage), but out of scope for MVP.
risks: Insufficient input validation can result in unsafe operations; mitigate by aggressive sanitizer hooks and staged rollout.
Too-flexible DSL may allow complex side effects; keep DSL minimal for MVP and iterate based on real templates.
Audit volume: structured telemetry could increase cardinality in metrics pipeline — aggregate judiciously and sample for heavy runs.
Operational complexity if compensating steps are not well-defined leading to manual cleanups.
Security review may require HSM/KMS integration for certain steps that access secrets; plan for extra time.
User training required: support engineers must learn dry-run and approval flows to avoid accidental runs.
If idempotency hints are incorrect, replays may have unintended consequences; require test coverage and review checklist.
